title: Cauchy Schwarz bound for the bilinear L2 test pairing
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] and Lebesgue measure on Euclidean $\mathbf R^m$, where $m\geq1$. Let $a,b:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf C$ be measurable and square-integrable, with $\|a\|_2=(\int|a|^2)^{1/2}$ and the analogous notation for $b$. Then $ab$ is integrable and $$\int|a(x)b(x)|\,dx\leq\|a\|_2\|b\|_2,\qquad\left|\int a(x)b(x)\,dx\right|\leq\|a\|_2\|b\|_2.$$ The pairing is bilinear, with no complex conjugation.
